modelAnswer:
When Coach Pitt said “Nice work!” to her at the finish line, Eva was surprised. Still breathing hard, she turned around and saw several classmates jogging behind her. She had not come in last after all. In fact, she had finished the whole mile without stopping. The mile had not grown any shorter. By breaking it into small parts, from the oak tree’s shadow to the curve of the track, she had turned a frightening task into something she could manage. Walking back toward the huge building, she thought of the endless hallways waiting inside.

Eva decided to use the same trick to deal with the school building. Instead of trying to remember all six floors at once, she would learn them one part at a time. That afternoon, she followed one hallway on the first floor and found the cafeteria, then took another to the gym. The next day, she explored the second floor and found the library. Each time she reached a new place, she added it to a simple map in her notebook. Within two weeks, the hallways no longer looked like a maze. She could now walk from her classroom to the laboratories without asking for directions. One morning, a lost new student asked her the way to the library. Eva smiled and led her there, one hallway at a time.

centralSituation.statement: 高一新生 Eva 开学第一周有两个难处：方向感差，找不到路，于是只记教室位置、假装楼里其他地方不存在；第一节体育课又被要求跑一英里，而这正是她最怕的事。跑步时她靠“只盯下一个小目标”的心理小把戏坚持下来。

evidence.excerpt: One of the major headaches for her was finding her way in the huge school building.
There was nothing she feared more than having to run a whole mile.
Feeling desperate, Eva started using a mind trick on herself.

sourceEndState.statement: 原文停在 Eva 已跑完第四圈：她不再想“一英里”，而是先跑到橡树影子、再到弯道、再完成一圈，一圈接一圈。原文没有交代她是否已到终点、名次如何；教学楼的问题仍被她“假装不存在”，没有解决。

evidence.excerpt: One lap turned into two, then three, then four.
She decided that she would memorize where her classes were and then pretend that the rest of the place didn’t exist.

evidence.excerpt: “It’s just the beginning,” she thought.
